title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Make polite requests, ask favours, invite, offer, accept and refuse gracefully — and use respectful language with elders.
intro:
Gujarati politeness lives mostly in the **verb form**, not in a word for 'please'. Compare **આપો** 'give', **આપજો** 'please give', **આપશો?** 'would you give?' and **આપ આપશો?** — each step is softer. Add **જરા** 'just a little' or the tag **ને** and you sound both polite and friendly.

Gujarati hospitality is legendary: be ready for **આગ્રહ** — the host insisting you eat more.

vocab.note: f · તકલીફ માટે માફ કરજો 'sorry for the trouble'
n · આપનું સ્વાગત છે 'you are welcome (here)'
m · તમને વાંધો ન હોય તો 'if you don't mind'
X ની રાહ જોવી 'to wait for X'

phrases.en: Could you give me some water?

phrases.native: તમે થોડી વાર રાહ જોઈ શકશો?
phrases.roman: tame thoḍī vār rāh joī shaksho?
phrases.en: Could you wait a little while?

phrases.native: તમને વાંધો ન હોય તો હું બારી ખોલું?
phrases.roman: tamne vāndho na hoy to huṃ bārī kholuṃ?
phrases.en: If you don't mind, shall I open the window?
Will you have tea or coffee?
No, thank you. I just had some.
At least take a little! Don't be shy.
Do come to our place for a meal on Sunday.
We'll certainly come — thanks for the invitation.

phrases.native: માફ કરજો, આ વખતે નહીં ફાવે.
phrases.roman: māf karjo, ā vakhate nahīṃ fāve.
phrases.en: Sorry, it won't be possible this time.

grammar.title: The politeness ladder for requests
grammar.body:
From blunt to very polite:

**આપ** (intimate imperative) — to a child or close friend
**આપો** (polite imperative) — normal with adults, fine in shops
**આપજો** (deferred imperative) — softer; also for instructions for later
**આપશો?** (future as a question) — 'would you give?', a courteous request
**આપી શકશો?** — 'could you give?', very polite
**આપ મને … આપશો?** — with આપ, extremely respectful

Softeners: **જરા** 'just', **ને** at the end ('do…'), **પ્લીઝ** (very common), and the formal **કૃપા કરીને** in writing and announcements. For refusals, Gujaratis avoid a bare **ના**: they say **નહીં ફાવે** 'it won't suit', **જોઈશું** 'we'll see', or give a reason.

examples.en: Please shut the door when you leave.
Would you mind shutting the door?

examples.native: આપ જરા અહીં સહી કરી શકશો?
examples.roman: āp jarā ahīṃ sahī karī shaksho?
examples.en: Could you kindly sign here? (very respectful)

grammar.title: The subjunctive: 'shall I…?', 'let's…', 'may…'
grammar.body:
The bare present forms without **છે** form the **subjunctive**, used for suggestions, permission and wishes:

હું કરું, તું કરે, એ કરે, અમે/આપણે કરીએ, તમે કરો, એ લોકો કરે.

**Shall I…? / May I…?** — **હું આવું?** 'May I come?', **ચા બનાવું?** 'Shall I make tea?'
**Let's…** — **આપણે જઈએ** or **ચાલો, જઈએ** 'let's go'
**Wishes and 'so that'** — after **કે** and **જેથી**: **મારી ઇચ્છા છે કે તમે આવો** 'I'd like you to come'
**Maybe** — **કદાચ એ આવે** 'he might come'
**Conditions** — **જો તમને વાંધો ન હોય** 'if you don't mind' (Unit 19).

examples.en: Shall I make you some tea?
Shall I drop you at the station?

dialogue.title: Visiting a friend's family
dialogue.setting: Tom visits his colleague Jignesh's home in Vadodara for the first time and meets his parents.

lines.speaker: Father
lines.en: Come in, come in! Welcome. Have a seat.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: નમસ્તે કાકા, નમસ્તે કાકી. આ તમારા માટે મીઠાઈ.
lines.roman: namaste kākā, namaste kākī. ā tamārā māṭe mīṭhāī.
lines.en: Hello uncle, hello auntie. These sweets are for you.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: અરે, આની શું જરૂર હતી? ચા લેશો કે શરબત?
lines.roman: are, ānī shuṃ jarūr hatī? chā lesho ke sharbat?
lines.en: Oh, there was no need! Will you have tea or sherbet?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: ચા, પ્લીઝ. ઓછી ખાંડ, જો તકલીફ ન હોય તો.
lines.roman: chā, plīz. ochhī khāṃḍ, jo taklīf na hoy to.
lines.en: Tea, please. Less sugar, if it's no trouble.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: એમાં શું તકલીફ? અને નાસ્તો પણ કરજો.
lines.roman: emāṃ shuṃ taklīf? ane nāsto paṇ karjo.
lines.en: What trouble? And do have some snacks too.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: બસ, થોડું જ. હમણાં જ જમીને આવ્યો છું.
lines.roman: bas, thoḍuṃ j. hamṇāṃ j jamīne āvyo chhuṃ.
lines.en: Just a little. I've just eaten.

lines.speaker: Father
lines.native: એવું ના ચાલે! થોડા ખાખરા તો લો.
lines.roman: evuṃ nā chāle! thoḍā khākhrā to lo.
lines.en: That won't do! At least have some khakhra.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: ભલે, આભાર. તમે મને જરા ગુજરાતી શીખવશો?
lines.roman: bhale, ābhār. tame mane jarā gujarātī shīkhavsho?
lines.en: All right, thanks. Would you teach me a bit of Gujarati?

lines.speaker: Father
lines.native: જરૂર! દર રવિવારે જમવા આવજો, ગુજરાતી પણ શીખી જશો.
lines.roman: jarūr! dar ravivāre jamvā āvjo, gujarātī paṇ shīkhī jasho.
lines.en: Of course! Come and eat every Sunday — you'll pick up Gujarati too.

culture: When visiting, bring sweets or fruit, take your shoes off at the door, and greet elders first — younger Gujaratis may touch an elder's feet (**પગે લાગવું**) on special occasions. Refusing food once is polite; the host will insist (**આગ્રહ**), and accepting a little the second time pleases everyone. Use **આપ** and plural verb forms for elders: **કાકા આવ્યા** 'uncle came', not *āvyo*.
